name: QNT
classificationNote: Classified by TypeSafe jev-1.13.0 (confidence 0.95). Replaced keyword guess "arbitrary-call".
rootCause: The QNT reserve pool exploit abused Ethereum's EIP-7702 delegation mechanism introduced in the Pectra upgrade. The reserve pool's admin EOA had delegated execution logic via EIP-7702 to a BatchExecutor contract, which further invoked a BatchCall contract. The critical flaw was that BatchCall.batch() was entirely public with zero access control — no onlyOwner, no whitelist, no require(msg.sender == ...) guard. Any external caller could supply arbitrary target addresses and calldata, which the contract executed unconditionally. The attacker exploited this open function to route a forged call through the EIP-7702-delegated admin EOA, causing it to satisfy the QNT pool's _isAdmin(msg.sender) check inside forwardTransaction(). This authorized a transfer of 1,988.5 QNT (~$125K) directly to the attacker's address. SlowMist detected the exploit and traced the root cause to the missing access control on the batch execution pathway. Attack Tx: 0x4f31f68df9f240492f13df9ab23207ea231ec1b5a89af9c31cde58e7d98cb18c Analysis: EIP-7702 Flaw Drains 1,988 QNT From Ethereum Pool — CryptoTimes Defi_Nerd_sec on X
